$comment: Full draft for Hitchwiki/hitchhiking-data-standard issue #44 (B72). Top-level record (this file's root type/properties) validates against STANDARD.md, fetched live 2026-08-18 (not from memory of an earlier run). All 11 sub-types in $defs were encoded in an earlier pass this run, re-checked here against a live re-fetch of each tags/*.md file where the top-level table's field names disagreed (see 'waiting_time' note on 'stops' below). Validated with the jsonschema library (4.26.0, installed into .state/jsonschema-venv since this machine has no jsonschema by default) against every worked example embedded in STANDARD.md and each tags/*.md file -- see the .md writeup for the run log, not just eyeballed this time.

version.description: Version of this standard being used, format x.y.z.

stops.description: At least one item required. First item marks the origin. If there is more than one item, the last item marks the destination and must not carry departure_time or a waiting duration.
stops.$comment: STANDARD.md's own prose says the destination item forbids 'departure_time or waiting_time' -- note the field is actually named waiting_duration everywhere else in the spec (tags/stop.md), a second documentation inconsistency alongside the hitchhiker.nickname/float bug found in the earlier pass; read as referring to waiting_duration. This 'last item, only if length>1' constraint is not enforced here: JSON Schema 2020-12 has no native way to constrain specifically the last element of a variable-length array (prefixItems only pins a fixed prefix), same gap already flagged inside $defs.stop itself. A conforming validator would need a custom keyword or a post-validation script step.

rating.description: Subjective rating of the spot where the ride started (or where the hitchhiker waited, for a no_ride).

hitchhikers.description: minItems 1 is an inference (STANDARD.md's prose says 'most often a solo hitchhiker' but never states a minimum explicitly) -- flagged, not silently assumed.

comment.description: Free-form comment about the starting location, destination, or the entire ride.

signals.description: Listed in the order used. STANDARD.md says the sum of each signal's duration must be <= the origin stop's waiting_duration -- a cross-object numeric constraint spanning two different array fields, not encoded here (same class of gap as the stops/no_ride note above).

no_ride.description: Presence marks the record as a completed no-ride attempt. When set: occupants, ride, and mode_of_transportation must be omitted (enforced below via the root-level if/then); stops 'should' contain exactly one item (STANDARD.md's own word is 'should', not 'must', so not enforced as a hard requirement here).

source.description: URL of the submitting application, or the literal string "private".

license.description: Lower-case license identifier. STANDARD.md gives apache-2.0, mit, cc-by-4.0, odbl as examples with a trailing '...', i.e. explicitly non-exhaustive -- not restricted to an enum here on purpose.

submission_time.description: RFC 9557 date-time when this record was submitted to source.

latitude.description: Latitude of a spot in decimal degrees.

longitude.description: Longitude of a spot in decimal degrees.

is_exact.description: Whether the location is placed exact or just roughly into a city, direction or region.

origin_location.description: The city where the person lives in or any other administrative unit smaller than country-level.

origin_country.description: Country where the person lives primarily. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

hitchhiker.$comment: Inherits from person (tags/hitchhiker.md: 'inherits from person'), so allOf + its own additional fields rather than duplicating person's fields. Uses unevaluatedProperties, not additionalProperties, at this level -- additionalProperties:false on a sibling allOf branch only sees that branch's own properties, so it would wrongly reject the *other* branch's legitimate fields when the two are combined; unevaluatedProperties is JSON Schema 2020-12's fix for exactly this, and person itself was changed to carry no additionalProperties of its own so this is the only gate. Caught by actually validating STANDARD.md's own worked hitchhiker/occupant examples (jsonschema 4.26.0), not by eyeballing -- the first-pass version of this schema had the bug.

nickname.description: Nickname of the hitchhiker, assumed unique within the scope of the `source` application. STANDARD.md's own source table types this 'float', which contradicts its own example ("Alice") -- treated as a documentation typo, encoded as string here, not copied blindly.

hitchhiking_since.description: The year the person hitchhiked for the first time.

description.description: Further description of the gift received.

price.description: [amount, currency]. If used, both values are required. currency uses ISO 4217 or common crypto codes (BTC, SATS). amount is a positive decimal number.

sign_content.description: Only if 'sign' is included in methods.

asking_content.description: Only if 'asking' is included in methods.

occupant.$comment: Inherits from person (tags/occupant.md: 'inherits from person'), same allOf + unevaluatedProperties pattern as hitchhiker (see its $comment for why additionalProperties would be wrong here).

license_plate_identifier.description: Location-based identifier on the plate, e.g. German city/district or French department.

vehicle_destination.description: Final destination of the vehicle ride, can be further than the hitchhiker's own ride.

stop.$comment: STANDARD.md's own 'stops' field says arrival_time/departure_time are not allowed on the last (destination) item -- that cross-item constraint lives at the record level (see the root 'stops' property's own $comment), not encodable inside a single stop's own schema, so not attempted here.
